description: Per-profile render frame budgets (R32-RENDER-BUDGETS, RFC 0005 'Performance and promotion'). Each row gates one workload on one product profile. Measured by tools/quality/frame_pacing.py (desktop) or tools/quality/frame_pacing_device.py (iOS/tvOS); the budgets apply to the scenario's last (warm) pass. Feature budgets stay with their owners (indirect-light-v1.json, RFC 0012 A0, RFC 0008 F10).

rows.target: a locked 60 fps at 1920x1080 (user direction, 2026-09-26), with the profile's render defaults
rows.set: 2026-09-26, before any optimization for this target

vsync.meaning: what a player sees: presented at the display's 60 Hz; no frame may hold the screen for a second refresh (frame_pacing.count_missed_refreshes)

headroom.meaning: the frame's own cost: GPU rendering and the presenting thread's CPU time each leave room under the 16.7 ms refresh

rows.status: pass (2026-09-26, one scenario): warm passes 0 missed refreshes, max 21.1 ms; GPU render p99 15.8 ms, CPU p99 12.2 ms. Thin margin (a vsync run read GPU p99 16.05 ms); other maps unmeasured.
rows.revised: 2026-09-26, after the first Apple TV measurements, while optimizing: the Apple TV presents only in FIFO, so 'vsync off' never measured headroom, and under vsync the CPU frame-start p99 flags jitter that still makes every refresh (a 20 ms interval followed by a 13 ms one). The row now counts missed refreshes and measures headroom as GPU render and CPU time. The first definition (p99 17.5 ms with vsync, 16.0 ms without) is in git history.

rows.presentation: 1920x1080 through SDL's offscreen driver (VK_EXT_headless_surface): the product's native Vulkan path on the same GPU and driver, without compositor pacing, vsync off, mat_queue_mode 0. A private headless mutter Wayland session paces presents at about 18 Hz (55 ms intervals with 5 ms of CPU; measured 2026-09-26), so it measures the compositor, not the frame; a real Wayland session is the user's desktop and is not used.
rows.target: a 120 fps median with every frame inside a 60 Hz refresh at p99
rows.set: set 2026-09-26 (RFC 0016 K0, agent decision under the user's standing instruction), before this row was measured; the render core's later gates also compare against this row's k0_record through the frame allowance

headroom.meaning: the frame's own cost with vsync off

rows.hardware: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold7 (SM-F971U1), Adreno 840, inner display
rows.presentation: fullscreen at the device's native resolution, vsync off, mat_queue_mode 0, the APK's defaults
rows.target: 60 fps: a median inside one refresh, p95 inside 1.5 refreshes, p99 inside two
rows.set: set 2026-09-26 (RFC 0016 K0, agent decision under the user's standing instruction), before this row was measured; the render core's later gates also compare against this row's k0_record through the frame allowance

headroom.meaning: the frame's own cost with vsync off

rows.revised: 2026-09-26, at the user's direction ("You can adjust the limits"), after the first Fold7 measurement: the first limits (p95 20.0, p99 25.0, GPU render p99 16.7, submission p99 12.0 ms) were missed by the product as it is (p95 23.8, p99 28.7, GPU render p99 18.1, submission p99 14.8 ms). The row now allows a frame to hold two refreshes at p99. The first definition is in git history.

pending_rows: None of R32-RENDER-BUDGETS's first two profiles is pending: the desktop Wayland and Fold7 rows are set (RFC 0016 K0).

metrics.p50_ms: warm-pass frame interval median (frame_pacing summary median_ms)
metrics.gpu_render_p99_ms: GPU time of the frame's rendering, 99th percentile (-vkframestats timestamps)
metrics.submission_p99_ms: main-thread submission time: the backend's draw emission on the main thread (emit, mat_queue_mode 0), 99th percentile

allowance.description: RFC 0016 frame allowance: a later render-core gate passes when the warm median is at most median x and p99 at most p99 x the row's k0_record on the same profile, unless a row records a tighter limit.
